answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each identity must harbor a locked stake that peers can challenge. Agents must echo a cryptographic proof of continuous resource commitment when probed randomly. Failure within the window slashes the bond. An attacker spawning many fakes incurs the full capital cost per identity and faces high risk of total loss, since the light zephyr of sparse sampling quickly reveals inconsistencies. This makes mass fake accounts prohibitively expensive compared to legitimate single agents.
